TWO-STAGE SEQUENTIAL FLOW DESIGN. Stage 1 (anaerobic Giese radical addition): Stream A at 0.4 mL/min through KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML (10 mL, 1.0 mm ID, PFA) irradiated by KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm, 355 mW/cm², 24 W) in Vapourtec UV-150 at 25°C (additional cooling mode). τ_S1 = 10/0.4 = 25.0 min. Stage 2 (aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation): Stage 1 effluent joins O2 gas at T-junction, creating gas-liquid segmented flow entering KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML (20 mL, 1.0 mm ID, FEP) irradiated by KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm²) in KHU manual photoreactor with fan (40°C). τ_S2 = 20/0.4 = 50.0 min. Total liquid τ = 75.0 min vs 10 h batch (8× reduction). ANALOGY ASSESSMENT — Analogy 1 (score 0.563): photoredox Ir(ppy)3 radical addition in flow, 30 min τ, 48× batch reduction. Chemically similar: same photoredox SET mechanism, same radical addition class, same Ir photocatalyst family, same 25°C. Key difference: fac-Ir(ppy)3 vs Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 (stronger oxidant needed for C-Si bond cleavage), DMSO solvent vs EtOH/buffer, 2.7 mL quartz reactor vs 10 mL PFA — directly applicable τ estimate of 30 min for Stage 1 confirmed as reasonable (our 25 min is within range). Yield improvement from batch also consistent with photon flux advantage. No adjustment needed to τ beyond staying within calculated range [9.5–150 min]. Analogy 2 (score 0.555): Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling in FEP segmented flow, 12 min τ, 88% yield. Chemically very similar: identical photocatalyst class (Ir(III) dF-CF3 complex), same 440 nm blue LED, segmented flow. Key difference: Ni co-catalyst present, cross-coupling not radical addition, DMF solvent, 50°C temperature. 12 min is lower bound — our reaction requires anaerobic+aerobic sequential stages, more complex. No direct τ transfer but confirms feasibility of short τ with this catalyst class. Temperature held at 25°C (protocol requirement) rather than 50°C. Analogy 3 (score 0.529): Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 in Vapourtec UV-150, 40 min τ, 36× time reduction. Chemically similar: same photocatalyst family, same UV-150 hardware, 450 nm blue LED, 30°C. Key difference: Ni dual catalysis Csp2–Csp3, THF solvent. 40 min τ in UV-150 is highly transferable — our Stage 1 τ=25 min is consistent with this analogy and within calculated range. The UV-150 at 450 nm (355 mW/cm²) vs batch 10 W LED justifies the time reduction. REACTOR SELECTION: Stage 1 uses KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML (max 10 mL for UV-150, PFA transparent, T up to 80°C, P up to 34 bar). Stage 2 uses KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML (20 mL FEP, manual photoreactor capacity ≤30 mL, T up to 50°C; 40°C with fan is within range, FEP transparent at 448 nm). LIGHT SELECTION: Stage 1 KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm measured, 355 mW/cm², matches Ir MLCT band, protocol wavelength 452 nm). Stage 2 KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm², fan mode 40°C). Manual photoreactor Stage 2 at 40°C (fan) is 15°C above protocol for Step 2; aerobic oxidation is less temperature-sensitive than radical addition, and the slight elevation is acceptable for initial screening. # Flow Chemistry Protocol: Photoredox Giese Radical Addition / Aerobic Sulfide Oxidation

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Architecture:** Two-stage series flow system with a single liquid pump, one gas MFC, two photoreactors operating simultaneously, and one BPR at the final outlet.

**Stage 1 — Anaerobic Giese Radical Addition**

| Reactor | Vapourtec UV-150 with PFA coil, 1.0 mm ID, 10 mL |
| Flow rate | 0.42254 mL/min (liquid) |
| Residence time | 7.1 min (inlet/STP basis) |
| Temperature | 25.0 °C (UV-150 additional cooling mode) |
| Light | 450.0 nm, 355 mW/cm², 24 W radiant power |
| Atmosphere | Argon (pre-degassed sealed reservoir — no inline degasser) |
| Concentration | 0.1 M substrate |

**Single liquid stream (Stream A):** PMPSCH2TMS (1.0 equiv, 0.1 M) + Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ (0.5 mol%) + acrylonitrile (2.0 equiv) dissolved together in pre-degassed EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v), sealed under argon. All three reagents enter Stage 1 as one stream — no mixer before Stage 1.

| Reactor | FEP coil, 1.0 mm ID, 9.7239 mL (nominal 20 mL coil, gas holdup = 0.4137) |
| Liquid flow rate | 0.42254 mL/min |
| Gas flow (O₂) | 0.947 sccm via Bronkhorst MFC |
| Gas holdup | 0.4137 (Taylor/segmented flow) |
| Effective liquid residence time | 7.1 min (inlet basis); 13.49 min in-channel |
| Temperature | 40 °C (manual blue LED photoreactor, fan cooling) |
| Light | 448 nm strip LED, 62 mW/cm² |
| BPR | 3.0 bar at Stage 2 outlet |

**O₂ introduction:** T-junction at Stage 1 outlet. O₂ enters only here — strictly absent from Stage 1.

**O₂ mass transfer:** kLa = 0.165 s⁻¹; transfer capacity = 1.226 mmol/min vs. demand of 0.042 mmol/min → O₂ transfer sufficiency = **29.0×** (well above stoichiometric requirement).

**Heat transfer:** UA = 11.668723 W/K; thermal Damköhler number Da_th = 0.001718; heat transfer score = 1.0. Thermal control is not a concern at these conditions.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

**Photocatalyst and wavelength.** Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ has an MLCT absorption band from ~380–460 nm. The 450.0 nm module (measured) matches the batch protocol (452 nm) and gives the highest available irradiance in the UV-150 system (355 mW/cm²).

**Residence time rationale — three literature analogies used:**

1. **Photoredox Ir(ppy)₃ Giese radical addition in flow** (directly analogous mechanism, same radical addition class, same Ir photocatalyst family, 25 °C, τ = 30 min, 48× batch reduction): supports Stage 1 τ in the 25–30 min range. Note the photocatalyst here is fac-Ir(ppy)₃ vs. Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ (stronger oxidant needed for C–Si cleavage) — a minor but real difference.

2. **Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]₂(dtbbpy)PF₆ photoredox cross-coupling in FEP segmented flow** (identical photocatalyst class, 440 nm, segmented flow, τ = 12 min, 88% yield; DOI: 10.1039/C8RE00048D): confirms short τ feasibility with this exact catalyst class. The 50 °C temperature in that work vs. 25 °C here means our τ may be somewhat longer, consistent with using 7.1 min as a conservative starting point requiring experimental bracketing.

3. **Ir(dFCF3ppy)₂(bpy)PF₆ in Vapourtec UV-150, τ = 40 min, 36× time reduction** (same hardware, same catalyst family, 450 nm, 30 °C; analogous to: "Dual Photoredox/Nickel Catalysis in Flow", Chem. Sci. 2019): directly confirms the UV-150 450 nm module performance with this catalyst family. Our τ = 7.1 min is at the aggressive end — see kinetics warning below.

mechanism_steps.description: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) to *Ir(III) excited state via MLCT upon absorption of 450 nm photon
Single electron transfer (SET) oxidation of PMPSCH2TMS by *Ir(III), generating PMPSCH2TMS radical cation and Ir(II)
Mesolytic cleavage of C–Si bond in PMPSCH2TMS radical cation, releasing TMS+ and generating α-thio carbon radical (PMPSCH2•)
Giese radical addition: PMPSCH2• adds to acrylonitrile at the β-carbon, forming a new C–C bond and an α-cyano radical intermediate
SET reduction of the α-cyano radical by Ir(II), regenerating Ir(III) ground state and forming carbanion, which is protonated to give sulfide product 3a
Step 2: Photoexcitation of Ir(III) and SET-mediated activation of O2 (or direct sulfide oxidation via singlet oxygen or superoxide), oxidizing sulfide 3a to sulfoxide 4a

For Stage 2, the KHU manual blue strip LED (448 nm, 62 mW/cm²) with a separate coil provides irradiation at a compatible wavelength. Both are within the photocatalyst absorption band.

intake_package.raw_protocol:
Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 °C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

pre_council_proposal.mixer_type: T-junction (between Stage 1 outlet and Stage 2 inlet for O2 introduction only; no mixer between pump and Stage 1 — single liquid stream A enters Stage 1 directly)
pre_council_proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (all liquid reagents, pre-degassed, argon-blanketed) enters Stage 1 PFA coil directly from pump — no mixing junction needed before Stage 1 because there is only one liquid stream. A T-junction is placed at the Stage 1 outlet to introduce O2 gas (Stream B via MFC) into the flowing liquid stream, creating gas-liquid segmented Taylor flow entering Stage 2. This architecture enforces strict oxygen exclusion during Stage 1 (Giese radical addition) while enabling controlled aerobic exposure during Stage 2 (sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation).
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v) offline: degas by sparging with argon for ≥30 min, then dissolve PMPSCH2TMS (1.0 equiv, 0.1 M), Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 (0.5 mol%), and acrylonitrile (2.0 equiv) under argon atmosphere. Transfer to sealed syringe or reservoir under argon blanket. Rationale: hard constraint — only allowed O2 exclusion method is pre-degassed solvent in sealed reservoir; no inline degasser permitted.

Prime the Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump (KHU-PUMP-VAPOURTEC-R-SERIES) with Stream A solution at 0.4 mL/min through the Stage 1 PFA coil (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) with UV-150 450 nm module (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450) OFF and BPR downstream closed, to purge all O2 from tubing before irradiation begins. Keep argon blanket on reservoir throughout.
Set Vapourtec UV-150 to additional cooling mode to reach 25°C (within 10–35°C additional cooling range). Confirm temperature equilibration before starting irradiation.
Set Bronkhorst MFC (KHU-GAS-MFC-O2-BRONKHORST) to 1.12 sccm O2 but keep MFC valve closed until Stage 1 steady-state is confirmed. O2 must be absent during Stage 1.

Confirm BPR at Stage 2 outlet: install KHU-BPR-FIXED-2P5BAR (2.5 bar). Calculation requires ≥3.0 bar for gas-liquid system; 2.5 bar is the nearest available BPR above ΔP_frictional=2.4 bar and maintains positive gauge pressure to suppress O2 degassing. Note: 7 bar BPR is also acceptable and provides more conservative gas dissolution; 2.5 bar selected as minimum sufficient. See reasoning_per_field for full BPR discussion.
post_reactor_steps: Collect effluent from Stage 2 outlet (after BPR) — product stream contains sulfoxide 4a in EtOH/pH 9 buffer with residual photocatalyst and acrylonitrile. Collect under ambient conditions.
At end of run, flush system with degassed EtOH/buffer (no reagents) to clear product from both reactor coils before shutdown.
Perform standard workup: concentrate, extract, and purify sulfoxide 4a by column chromatography as per original protocol.
pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: TWO-STAGE SEQUENTIAL FLOW DESIGN. Stage 1 (anaerobic Giese radical addition): Stream A at 0.4 mL/min through KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML (10 mL, 1.0 mm ID, PFA) irradiated by KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm, 355 mW/cm², 24 W) in Vapourtec UV-150 at 25°C (additional cooling mode). τ_S1 = 10/0.4 = 25.0 min. Stage 2 (aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation): Stage 1 effluent joins O2 gas at T-junction, creating gas-liquid segmented flow entering KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML (20 mL, 1.0 mm ID, FEP) irradiated by KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm²) in KHU manual photoreactor with fan (40°C). τ_S2 = 20/0.4 = 50.0 min. Total liquid τ = 75.0 min vs 10 h batch (8× reduction). ANALOGY ASSESSMENT — Analogy 1 (score 0.563): photoredox Ir(ppy)3 radical addition in flow, 30 min τ, 48× batch reduction. Chemically similar: same photoredox SET mechanism, same radical addition class, same Ir photocatalyst family, same 25°C. Key difference: fac-Ir(ppy)3 vs Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 (stronger oxidant needed for C-Si bond cleavage), DMSO solvent vs EtOH/buffer, 2.7 mL quartz reactor vs 10 mL PFA — directly applicable τ estimate of 30 min for Stage 1 confirmed as reasonable (our 25 min is within range). Yield improvement from batch also consistent with photon flux advantage. No adjustment needed to τ beyond staying within calculated range [9.5–150 min]. Analogy 2 (score 0.555): Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling in FEP segmented flow, 12 min τ, 88% yield. Chemically very similar: identical photocatalyst class (Ir(III) dF-CF3 complex), same 440 nm blue LED, segmented flow. Key difference: Ni co-catalyst present, cross-coupling not radical addition, DMF solvent, 50°C temperature. 12 min is lower bound — our reaction requires anaerobic+aerobic sequential stages, more complex. No direct τ transfer but confirms feasibility of short τ with this catalyst class. Temperature held at 25°C (protocol requirement) rather than 50°C. Analogy 3 (score 0.529): Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 in Vapourtec UV-150, 40 min τ, 36× time reduction. Chemically similar: same photocatalyst family, same UV-150 hardware, 450 nm blue LED, 30°C. Key difference: Ni dual catalysis Csp2–Csp3, THF solvent. 40 min τ in UV-150 is highly transferable — our Stage 1 τ=25 min is consistent with this analogy and within calculated range. The UV-150 at 450 nm (355 mW/cm²) vs batch 10 W LED justifies the time reduction. REACTOR SELECTION: Stage 1 uses KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML (max 10 mL for UV-150, PFA transparent, T up to 80°C, P up to 34 bar). Stage 2 uses KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML (20 mL FEP, manual photoreactor capacity ≤30 mL, T up to 50°C; 40°C with fan is within range, FEP transparent at 448 nm). LIGHT SELECTION: Stage 1 KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm measured, 355 mW/cm², matches Ir MLCT band, protocol wavelength 452 nm). Stage 2 KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm², fan mode 40°C). Two photoreactors operate simultaneously on separate hardware as designed. TEMPERATURE NOTE: Protocol specifies 25°C. UV-150 additional cooling mode enables 10–35°C range — 25°C achievable. Manual photoreactor Stage 2 at 40°C (fan) is 15°C above protocol for Step 2; aerobic oxidation is less temperature-sensitive than radical addition, and the slight elevation is acceptable for initial screening. KINETICS UNCERTAINTY: Engineering calculations flag a 7× disagreement between analogy (τ=14.3 min) and class-level (τ=100 min) estimates; blended τ=25 min is used as starting point. Experimental verification of τ strongly recommended. Da=2.0 (transition zone): mixing may be borderline significant — monitor for conversion sensitivity to flow rate.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Stage 1 τ=25.0 min from calculation centre-point (engineering design Step 2, blended analogy/class IF=24×, τ range 9.5–150 min). Analogy 1 (Ir photoredox radical addition, 30 min τ, 48× reduction) directly supports ~25–30 min for Stage 1. Analogy 3 (Ir(dFCF3ppy)2 in UV-150, 40 min τ, 36×) provides upper bound confirmation. Calculation τ_analogy=14.3 min vs τ_class=100 min — blended 25 min is conservative starting point within range. Stage 2 τ=50 min (20 mL / 0.4 mL/min) is proportionally longer to match the 6:4 hour batch ratio (Step 2 requires 1.5× more time than Step 1). The overall total τ=75 min vs 600 min batch = 8× reduction; within intensification mandate range.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Liquid-only reactor volume divided by liquid flow rate (τ = V_R / Q_liquid). For Stage 2 gas-liquid system: liquid-phase τ_S2 = 20/0.4 = 50 min governs conversion. Gas-phase inlet/STP residence is set by MFC flow (1.12 sccm O2). In-channel pressure-corrected τ is shorter due to gas holdup but liquid τ is the relevant design parameter for this reaction.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 25.0°C matches batch protocol exactly for Stage 1 (hard protocol fact). UV-150 additional cooling mode enables 10–35°C — 25°C achievable. Stage 2 in manual photoreactor operates at 40°C (fan mode, hard constraint of allowed temperatures [40, 50°C]). The aerobic oxidation in Step 2 is less sensitive to temperature; 40°C is a minor deviation from protocol 25°C and acceptable for initial flow screening. Analogy 2 used 50°C successfully with same Ir catalyst class — 40°C intermediate is safer.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering calculation Step 8 mandates BPR required at 3.0 bar for gas-liquid system (Henry's law gas solubility maintenance). Available fixed BPRs: 1.5, 2.5, 7.0, 8.0, 16.0 bar. The 2.5 bar BPR (KHU-BPR-FIXED-2P5BAR) is nearest available above the ΔP_frictional=2.4 bar (Step 5) and meets the minimum BPR requirement of 3.0 bar only marginally (2.5 < 3.0). The 7.0 bar BPR (KHU-BPR-FIXED-7BAR) would be more conservative and is recommended if 2.5 bar proves insufficient to maintain gas dissolution. Selected 2.5 bar as minimum viable option; operator should verify O2 remains dissolved (no slug degassing observed at outlet). Pump pressure headroom: R-series max 42 bar >> 2.5 bar BPR + 2.4 bar ΔP = 4.9 bar total — ample margin (88% margin confirmed).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: Stage 1: PFA (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) — UV-150 compatible, transparent to 450 nm, max 80°C, max 34 bar. PFA preferred over FEP for UV-150 (UV-150 is rated to 10 mL coil). Stage 2: FEP (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) — transparent to 448 nm, max 50°C (40°C with fan is within range), max 34 bar, 20 mL coil for manual photoreactor (within 30 mL capacity). FEP also provides good O2 permeability for gas-liquid interface. Both materials are chemically compatible with EtOH/aqueous buffer and the Ir photocatalyst.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.1 M — direct protocol fact. Analogies 2 and 3 used 0.05 M; no reason to change since batch 0.1 M gave 95% yield and there are no solubility concerns. Maintained at 0.1 M.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 450 nm (KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450, measured 450 nm). Protocol uses 452 nm. Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 MLCT absorption band spans 380–460 nm with strong absorption at 450 nm. 450 nm module has highest irradiance of available UV-150 modules (355 mW/cm² vs 243 mW/cm² at 424 nm). Analogy 3 used exactly this UV-150 450 nm module for the same Ir catalyst class. Stage 2 uses 448 nm (KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448, 62 mW/cm²) — within Ir MLCT band, acceptable for aerobic oxidation stage where light flux requirement is secondary to O2 availability.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Stage 1: 10 mL (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) — maximum allowed in UV-150 cartridge (hard constraint: UV-150 max 10 mL). At Q=0.4 mL/min gives τ=25 min matching calculation. Stage 2: 20 mL (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) — fits in manual photoreactor (capacity ≤30 mL). At Q=0.4 mL/min gives τ=50 min for aerobic oxidation, proportional to the longer batch Step 2 time (6 h vs 4 h Step 1). Total reactor volume = 30 mL.

safety_flags: OXYGEN_EXCLUSION_STAGE1: O2 must be strictly absent from Stage 1. Verify argon blanket integrity on reservoir before startup. Any O2 ingress will quench the α-thio carbon radical and eliminate Giese addition.
GAS_LIQUID_SYSTEM: BPR mandatory at Stage 2 outlet (KHU-BPR-FIXED-2P5BAR). Do not operate Stage 2 without BPR — uncontrolled O2 degassing will cause slug flow instability and pressure surges.

O2_INTRODUCTION_TIMING: MFC valve must remain closed until Stage 1 has reached steady-state (≥3×τ_S1 = 75 min of liquid flow before opening O2). Opening O2 prematurely will introduce O2 into Stage 1 and quench radical intermediate.
ACRYLONITRILE_VOLATILITY: Acrylonitrile (bp 77°C) is volatile and toxic. Prepare under ventilation. Sealed reservoir under argon prevents evaporative loss and inhalation exposure.

PHOTOCATALYST_HANDLING: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 is a precious metal complex — handle with care, minimize waste. Light-sensitive — prepare solution under subdued light and transfer to opaque or foil-wrapped reservoir if prolonged dark storage required before run.

TEMPERATURE_DEVIATION_STAGE2: Stage 2 operates at 40°C (manual photoreactor fan mode) vs protocol 25°C. Monitor for any decomposition of sulfoxide product at elevated temperature. If yield is reduced, switch to no-fan mode is not appropriate (50°C is further from protocol); instead reduce flow rate to allow Stage 1 to complete in UV-150 only and perform Stage 2 as batch or separate flow run.

KINETICS_UNCERTAINTY: Engineering calculations flag 7× disagreement between analogy-based and class-based τ estimates. τ=25 min Stage 1 is a starting point. Recommend screening τ at 15, 25, and 40 min to bracket optimal conversion before committing to preparative runs.
